conviction_note: The findings net to +0.5 (impact_sum). The scaled number is (2*0.55-1)*15 = +1.5. It leans slightly long for four reasons: the stock fell about 41% in a month, mostly in sector-wide AI-hardware sell-offs (Oct 14-15 inflation and SOX -4.3%; Nov 4 midterm 'data-center backlash'), not on company news; AMD guided its Oct-Dec quarter +27% q/q with Helios scale 'increasing substantially', and Sanmina's next-gen AMD program starts in that quarter; every EMS/ODM peer that reported this cycle beat and raised; and short interest is low. Two things hold p_up near 50. This name sold a beat-and-raise -17.5% last time because the guide lagged the Street. And consignment plus the cut ZT contribution make the reported-revenue optics of the FQ1 guide hard to call. The two measurements agree in sign, and both are small next to a 13.5% implied move.
bar: Fiscal Q4 FY26 (Jul-Sep 2026). Consensus revenue $3.48bn and non-GAAP EPS $3.27, per Zacks and Earnings Whispers (two agreeing sources: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/SANM/22671, 2026-11-02; finviz EPS next Q 3.27, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=SANM, 2026-11-09). Earnings Whispers puts the whisper at $3.41. Company guide: revenue $3.3-3.6bn, non-GAAP op margin 7.5-8.0%, EPS $3.05-3.35 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000897723/000089772326000036/sanmina_exx991xjune272026.htm, 2026-07-27). Consensus sits just above the guide midpoint ($3.45bn / $3.20). No sourced consensus exists for the FQ1 FY27 guide, which is the line the stock will most likely trade on. The only reference is management's reaffirmed 'more than $16bn' FY27 revenue target against a FY26 guide of $14.0-14.3bn.
positioning_check: Short float 3.30%, short ratio 2.47 days (finviz, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=SANM, read 2026-11-09). Equibles had 2.8% of float and 1.5 days on 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/sanm/shortinterest). The short is not crowded. Skew is +3.5 vol points (puts slightly bid) and put/call open interest is 0.2, so the book is call-heavy. Event-implied move is 13.49%; the 18.42% straddle carries 128% ATM IV. Run-up is -7.76% over 5 days and -31.3% over 20 days, -48% from the 52-week high and +19.5% off the low. The stock is bouncing about 9% intraday today ($146.83 against $134.68 on Nov 6, GuruFocus). Institutions own about 93%. Insiders have net-sold $42.9M over 12 months, and two Form 4s were filed since August (EDGAR).

findings.finding: AMD reported on 2026-11-03 and guided its Oct-Dec 2026 quarter to about $17bn revenue (+27% q/q, from $13.4bn). It said Helios rack-scale deployment 'will increase substantially in the fourth quarter', began volume shipments of the MI455X, and built about $3bn of inventory. AMD is the customer behind Sanmina's ZT Systems manufacturing business and its next-generation AMD-based accelerated-compute program, which management in July pushed out of FQ4 into FQ1 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), the quarter Sanmina guides tonight. That supports a sequential step-up in the FQ1 guide and a reaffirmed or raised FY27 'more than $16bn' target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: Q3 beat ($3.31 against $2.77 EPS) and a raised FY guide, but the Q4 revenue guide lagged the Street and the ZT contribution was cut. Stock -17.46%, and JPM cut its target the same day. April 2026: +14.56%. January 2026: -21.56%, on a weak revenue outlook. The guide line has driven every large move.
findings.why_not_priced: AMD reported six days ago, and SANM fell about 11% the next day in the midterm sell-off and kept falling to about $123-135. If the market were pricing AMD's Q4 rack ramp into Sanmina, SANM would have tracked AMD's post-print move, not sold off with data-center operators. Sanmina has not spoken since July, so consensus for its FQ1 predates AMD's Q4 guide.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/413880/sanminas-margin-gains-face-a-test-as-investors-look-past-q4-to-the-ai-ramp, 2026-11-02) confirms the next-gen AMD program ramp is 'slated to begin in fiscal Q1 2027'. Sanmina's Q3 release (sec.gov exx991, 2026-07-27): 'growth ramping throughout the year and into fiscal 2028.' Caveat, netted into the size: management said most FY27 ZT volume is consigned (factorstoday summary of filings, https://www.factorstoday.com/research/SANM, 2026-09-11), so reported revenue understates the program; Sanmina is AMD's preferred NPI partner without exclusivity; and the core business (about $9.1-9.2bn, +12.6%) has to hold.

findings.finding: Every EMS/ODM peer that reported the Jul-Sep 2026 quarter beat and most raised. Celestica: Q3 revenue $5.83bn against about $5.40-5.46bn estimates, above the high end of its guide, with 2027 'accelerating revenue growth'. Flex (Oct 28): beat, raised FY27 revenue to $34.9-35.9bn, Cloud & Power +54% y/y, CPI guided +75-85%. Super Micro (Nov 3): $19.9bn against $16.4bn consensus, FY27 raised to $72-82bn. Sanmina's core comms/cloud/AI business grew 33% last quarter and its FQ4 covers the same months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sanmina beat Q3 EPS by about 20% and fell 17.5%. Peers' beats were also sold this cycle: Celestica fell 14.4% in the week after its beat-and-raise (Zacks), though it rose 8.4% on Oct 28 (Trefis). Jabil fell premarket on Sept 30 after a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Sanmina's consensus of $3.48bn sits near the guide midpoint, not near the top, even though peers cleared their high ends. If the read-through were in the number, Street revenue would sit at or above $3.55bn, as the $3.41 EPS whisper only partly does.
findings.independence: Flex: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3017125/flex-q2-earnings-beat-estimates-on-cpi-strength-outlook-raised (2026-10-28). SMCI: https://finviz.com/news/414772/supermicro-announces-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results (2026-11-03). These are peers, not counterparties, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: In late-October Q3 reports, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft raised or held 2026 capex. Combined 2026 spend is about $803-828bn. Alphabet ('increase significantly in 2027') and Amazon ('meaningfully more in 2027') both signalled more for 2027. That supports Sanmina's FY27 cloud/AI demand framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no Sanmina-specific history on capex read-throughs. The stock sold off through October despite these prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced into the AI complex. It is filed because Sanmina fell 41% in the same month that end-demand series rose, which suggests the de-rating was financing, political and rate fear, not demand.
findings.independence: https://finimize.com/content/ai-infrastructure-stocks-took-a-beating-in-october (Oct 2026): orders at Vertiv, Schneider and ABB at records while their shares fell. This is a proxy; no Sanmina customer named.

findings.finding: The roughly 41% one-month drawdown (GuruFocus Nov 6: $134.68, 52-week low $118.10, against $218.55 on Sept 11) lines up with two sector-wide events and no company-level news. Oct 14-15: SOX -4.3% and -3.6% on hot inflation data and data-center-financing worries; SANM -8.25% and -7.9%. Nov 4: the Democratic midterm sweep hit data-center names, with Finviz headlining 'midterm data-center backlash sinks Sanmina 11% as Flex, Celestica and Jabil tumble'. Sanmina's only 8-K since July is a director appointment (Shanker Trivedi, ex-NVIDIA SVP). Forward P/E is 9.6x and the stock trades about 12x the FY26 EPS guide midpoint of $12.05.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026 (-21.6%) and July 2026 (-17.5%) both came off already-weak tapes, so a de-rated setup has not stopped this name from falling further on a soft guide.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. A finding about the macro cause of a drawdown is close to 'it is cheap'. The only edge claimed is that the cause was sector-wide, not a company leak. If it had been a leak (a lost program, an AMD shift to another builder), EDGAR, AMD's call or the peer prints would show it, and none of them do.
findings.independence: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9182657/sanmina-corp-sanm-shares-surge-34-what-gf-score-of-94-tells-investors (2026-11-06). EDGAR submissions (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000897723.json): only 8-K item 5.02 on 2026-09-15 since the print. Caveat: lesson 5 says an unexplained drawdown is worth 0, so this is sized small.

findings.finding: Q3's 8.0% non-GAAP operating margin was helped by pre-production NRE engineering fees that may not recur. Q4 is guided at 7.5-8.0% against a 6-7% long-term framework. Q3 operating cash flow was $124M (against $399M before) and free cash flow $24M after $101M of capex, with working capital building ahead of the ramp. Long-term debt is $1.96bn (against $283M a year earlier) and quarterly interest $32M (against $5M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July the margin beat (8.0% against an outlook below it) did not protect the stock: -17.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The facts are public since July. What is unpriced is whether FQ4 margin holds at or above 7.75% without the NRE. Earnings Whispers flags 'a drop toward the mid-6% range would suggest one-time help'. The financing question has an answer: the debt paid for ZT and the inventory build funds the AMD ramp, so the debt itself is not signed negative. The risk is cash conversion.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview, https://finviz.com/news/413880/sanminas-margin-gains-face-a-test-as-investors-look-past-q4-to-the-ai-ramp (2026-11-02). Simply Wall St flags the $2.2bn inventory build, https://www.webull.com/news/15852969812401152 (2026-11-02).

findings.finding: ZT Systems' contribution is shrinking and becoming consigned. ZT revenue was about $1.88bn in FQ2 and about $1.1bn in FQ3, and is guided to $0.8-1.0bn in FQ4 because legacy storage and general-purpose compute programs shifted. Management expects most FY27 ZT volume to use consigned components, which cuts reported revenue. Earnings Whispers adds that memory and custom-ASIC shortages could affect the $16bn FY27 goal. Together these raise the risk that tonight's FQ1 revenue guide reads light against a Street model built on gross revenue, even if profit dollars hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Exactly this line (ZT Q4 cut and the next-gen program moved out) drove the July -17.46% despite the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced by the drawdown. What is not priced is how much consignment cuts the FQ1 revenue guide: no sourced FQ1 consensus exists, and Street FY27 EPS at about $13.94 (Zacks) implies the market still models growth. If it were fully priced, the FY27 revenue estimate would sit below $16bn.
findings.independence: https://www.factorstoday.com/research/SANM (2026-09-11; ZT by quarter, consignment, no exclusivity). TrendForce: server DRAM undersupplied in 4Q26, https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260930-13258.html (2026-09-30). The memory point is a proxy. This finding offsets finding 1 in part, but on reported-revenue optics, not demand.

findings.finding: The reported-quarter bar sits above the guide. Consensus EPS of $3.27 is above the $3.20 midpoint, and the Earnings Whispers whisper of $3.41 is above the $3.35 top of the range, so an in-line print at the high end reads as a miss against the whisper.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 EPS beat the top of the guide and the stock still fell 17.5%. The EPS line has not paid on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Whisper above the top of the range means the buy side expects a beat; a merely in-line print would be visibly short of it.
findings.independence: This shares its document with finding 6. Finviz EPS next Q 3.27 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=SANM) confirms consensus.

findings.finding: Sanmina bought back no shares in FQ3, leaving about $600M of authorization unused (Trefis, Aug 26). With the stock down about 40% from September, any resumed buyback or new authorization tonight would be a capital-return positive. Leverage (about $1.96bn of LT debt) limits the size.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The pause was followed by a pullback (Trefis headline). There is no record of a reaction to a buyback announcement on a print.
findings.why_not_priced: Optional and undisclosed. If the market expected a resumption, the authorization would be cited in previews, and it is not.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly long, against a mildly positive skew (+3.5, puts bid) and a -31% 20-day run-up. The lean agrees with the call-heavy open interest and the low short float. The skew is small, so the sign is not fighting a strong market statement, but this name's history of selling good prints on a lagging guide keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest) and lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the AMD/next-gen finding went from +2.5 to +2.0, because it rests on one customer, is consigned and non-exclusive, and a July beat-and-raise was sold 17.5%.
Lesson 1 (this name sells its beats): the peer read-through on the reported quarter went from +1.0 to +0.7.

Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the drawdown/sector-cause positioning finding went from +0.5 to +0.3; it is kept because the cause is sourced to two sector events, not inferred from absence.
Lesson 5 (proxy) left the hyperscaler capex proxy at +0.7 and lesson 7 (positioning) left the negatives unchanged, since short interest is 3.3% and not crowded.
Lesson 9 also removed a draft finding on memory shortages, merged into finding 6 as one concern on the same guide line (the draft count of 9 already reflected this merge, so the count is unchanged).
